A1.justification: Both PDFs describe REPOCOD and provide readable main text, tables, figures, and appendices. Their contents can be matched despite substantial reorganization and revised statistics.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of ten LLMs, repository-specific results, retrieval analyses, and code-generation case studies.

after.justification: V4 retains original evaluations and adds context controls, failure analyses, REPOCOD-LITE results, and an OpenHands experiment.

M1.justification: The proposed construction pipeline retains repository filtering, static/dynamic function discovery, and assertion-failure replacement for test selection. The original retrieval procedures remain; new context controls and output filtering serve evaluation and analysis.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Python whole-function generation using 980 tasks from the same 11 repositories. REPOCOD-LITE selects 200 existing tasks, and OpenHands is evaluated on that subset; these preserve the represented task coverage.

E2.justification: V4 adds no-context, Callees, and Dense-oracle comparisons for GPT-4o and GPT-4o-Mini, plus OpenHands with Claude-3.5 Sonnet on REPOCOD-LITE. The recall-stratified comparison changes from ten models with dense retrieval to four commercial models with both BM25 and dense retrieval. The main ten-model comparison is retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include canonical-solution retrieval queries, callee context plus 1,024 prefix tokens, difficulty-ranked and category-balanced selection of 200 LITE tasks, and one-round OpenHands evaluation. Recall analysis changes from four bins to three, and new analyses specify complexity bins, output filtering, and a 30-task failure sample.

E4.justification: V1 already analyzes context complexity, solution length, retrieval recall, and individual examples. V4 substantially extends this with cyclomatic-complexity and dependency-count analyses, context controls, syntax-error analysis, a 30-failure audit, and comparisons of raw versus filtered generation length.

E5.justification: Both main evaluations use one greedily decoded output per model, task, and setting. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests; v4's additional analyses do not introduce such reporting.

E6.justification: Context-category counts change from 257/316/407 in v1 Table 1 to 498/177/305 in v4 Table 6; retrieval recalls and generation-length ratios also change. New results include GPT-4o's 28.6% under Dense-oracle, a 9.0% best LITE score, and 5.5% for OpenHands with Claude. The original headline and per-repository model scores are retained apart from rounding.

T1.justification: Appendix A.10 introduces a numerical difficulty definition for LITE selection: the product of prompt length and canonical-solution length, measured in lines of code. This is a limited mathematical scoring addition; no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central benchmark and below-30% performance claims remain. V4 adds prominent claims about reducing evaluation time to 10.4%, dependency-only context being suboptimal, and context helping self-contained tasks. Its contributions also emphasize large repository scale and increase the claimed repository-dependent proportion from 26.22% to 50.8%.

C2.justification: V4 interprets oracle comparisons as evidence that task descriptions already support effective retrieval and that dependencies alone are insufficient context. It adds explanations involving repetitive generation, helper functions, input validation, and incorrect core logic, while explicitly qualifying oracle settings as unrealistic. The existing repository-count and model-count limitations remain.

D1.justification: V4 adds the October 2024 repository snapshot date, explicit retrieval-corpus/query descriptions, context-prefix and output-filtering details, LITE selection instructions, and execution timings. The original prompting, greedy decoding, and API/HuggingFace/vLLM setup remain, with no concrete change in code or data release availability documented.

R1.justification: V4 substantially expands positioning through DevEval, RepoEval, R2E-Eval1, version-aware benchmarks, and SWE-Gym, while removing ClassEval's prominent comparison role. A new automated-test-collection subsection contrasts the proposed pipeline with prior approaches, extending the novelty argument beyond v1's benchmark discussion.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, with four benchmark criteria replacing three. Related work moves after results, prompting and detailed statistics move to the appendix, and the results narrative is reorganized around additional findings.

P2.justification: Several original figures and tables move to the appendix. Benchmark-comparison tables are expanded and reformatted, the complexity figure becomes three panels, and new displays cover context controls, syntax errors, filtered lengths, dependency counts, failure cases, and LITE results.

improvement.justification: V4's context controls, failure diagnostics, and measured test-selection savings improve the interpretation and practical value of v1's results. However, unexplained dependency reclassification and inconsistent appendix reporting limit the gain: Tables 6 and 13 list seven file-level plotly.py tasks in the full benchmark but fourteen in its LITE subset. The added evidence supports a positive, limited net improvement.
